items.title: Plas Johnson interviewed by Monk Rowe, Sarasota, Florida, April 12, 1996
items.q: Like we played behind artists, like Bobby Day or Larry Williams

ctx.x: Yeah. You’d just go and listen to the tune basically and find your part. Did the producers often have an idea of what they wanted you to do?

Yeah, usually. Either the producer or the artist. Like we played behind artists, like Bobby Day or Larry Williams who did “Bony Maronie”; Bobby Day did “Rockin’ Robin” and what else — they did pretty well. And artists like that had a whole concept of what they wanted the band to do and we did it. They would sing riffs and stuff to us and show us how the song goes and everything. And it usually came together in three hours.
Was there a time when you were driving in your car — did you have a car?
